Part two. Blockbuster. In two thousand, Netflix was losing money. So Hastings and Randolph flew to Dallas, to meet Blockbuster's boss. Their offer? Buy Netflix for fifty million dollars. Randolph later said the Blockbuster team could barely stop themselves from laughing. The answer was no. In two thousand four, Blockbuster was at its peak. More than nine thousand stores. Then the world changed. Red kiosks rented DVDs for one dollar a night. And in two thousand seven, Netflix started streaming. No store. No waiting. Just press play. Blockbuster was drowning in debt. In September twenty ten, the company filed for bankruptcy. By twenty fourteen, almost every Blockbuster on Earth had shut its doors. Except one. In Bend, Oregon, the last Blockbuster on the planet is still open. And Netflix, the company Blockbuster could have bought for fifty million dollars, is now worth hundreds of billions.
